name: ROLM Corporation
description: Acquired ROLM, a maker of PBX telephone equipment and military computers. IBM sold ROLM to Siemens in 1988 after the business underperformed.

name: Lotus Development Corporation
description: Acquired Lotus for its Notes collaboration platform, which became IBM's foundation for enterprise messaging and collaboration software.

name: Tivoli Systems, Inc.
description: Acquired Tivoli to build IBM's systems management and IT operations software portfolio, now a core part of IBM Automation.

name: Sequent Computer Systems
description: Acquired Sequent for its NUMA (non-uniform memory access) parallel server technology, strengthening IBM's high-end UNIX server line.

name: Informix Database Business
description: Acquired Informix's database software business from IBM's rival, significantly expanding DB2 market share. The Informix database products were rebranded under the DB2 family.

name: PricewaterhouseCoopers Consulting
description: Acquired PwC's consulting arm — 30,000 consultants — instantly creating one of the world's largest IT services businesses. Foundation of what is now IBM Consulting, generating $21B+ annually.

name: Rational Software
description: Acquired Rational for its software development tools (UML, requirements management, testing). Now IBM Engineering Lifecycle Management (ELM), used in aerospace, defense, and automotive.

name: PC Division → Lenovo
description: Sold the ThinkPad PC business to China's Lenovo for $1.75B. IBM retained an 18.9% stake in Lenovo. Strategic exit from commoditizing PC hardware to refocus on higher-margin enterprise technology.

name: DataMirror Corporation
description: Acquired DataMirror for its real-time data replication and integration technology, enhancing IBM's data management portfolio.

name: Cognos
description: Acquired the world's leading business intelligence and performance management software company. Became the foundation of IBM Cognos Analytics, now part of IBM's AI & Analytics portfolio.

name: SPSS
description: Acquired SPSS, the leading statistical analysis software used in academia, government, and business research. Now IBM SPSS Statistics.

name: Softlayer Technologies
description: Acquired SoftLayer, a cloud computing infrastructure provider, to establish IBM's global cloud delivery platform. Became the foundation of IBM Cloud.

name: Merge Healthcare
description: Acquired Merge Healthcare for its medical imaging and clinical data management capabilities, strengthening IBM Watson Health.

name: Truven Health Analytics
description: Acquired Truven Health Analytics, a leading provider of healthcare data and analytics, for Watson Health. One of IBM's largest healthcare investments.

name: Red Hat, Inc.
description: IBM's largest acquisition ever — the largest software acquisition in history at the time. Red Hat's open-source hybrid cloud platform became IBM's defining strategic bet under Arvind Krishna, who led the deal as SVP of Cloud.

name: Kyndryl Spin-off
description: Spun off IBM's managed infrastructure services business as an independent public company (NYSE: KD). IBM's largest-ever divestiture by revenue — Kyndryl had ~$19B in annual revenue at separation. The spinoff allowed IBM to refocus entirely on hybrid cloud and AI.

name: Apptio
description: Acquired Apptio, the leading Technology Business Management (TBM) and FinOps software platform, to help enterprises optimize technology spending. IBM's largest acquisition since Red Hat.

name: StreamSets & webMethods (from Software AG)
description: Acquired Software AG's data integration and API management platforms, strengthening IBM's hybrid integration portfolio for AI-ready data pipelines.

name: HashiCorp
description: Acquired HashiCorp, the leading multi-cloud infrastructure automation platform (Terraform, Vault, Consul). Extends IBM's hybrid cloud platform with best-in-class infrastructure-as-code capabilities.
